Gavrilov's compact stationary Euler flow and Constantin–La–Vicol's localizable Grad–Shafranov construction are important precedents for nonlinear compact pressure. Their constraint `u.grad p=0` and stationary Euler balance are different from Lemma 3.3, which permits a nonzero compact solenoidal acceleration and realizes prescribed rigid rotations on a plateau. No statement that compact pressure itself is new is made. [Brandolese–Meyer](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.1051/cocv:2002021.pdf), Remark 2.6 and Corollary 2.7, also give higher-moment polynomial-divisibility obstructions; Theorem 3.1 and Section 4 relate their persistence and discrete symmetries to improved algebraic spatial decay. Both quadratic isotropy and the general hierarchy of moment obstructions are prior ideas. The finite-mode control theorem of [Brandolese–Okabe](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.12733) uses a matrix divergence-form force and small initial data; its rapid dissipation is the stated little-oh energy rate, not compact velocity and pressure with all-order temporal decay. The proposed contribution here is the explicit finite all-moment cancellation compatible with an active rotation plateau, followed by the small-angle gate estimate. The fourth-harmonic test explains why imposing only quadratic isotropy or cubic symmetry would leave a real gap.
